html:
Tamar was queen of Georgia from 1184 to 1213, the first woman to rule Georgia in her own right, whose reign marked the height of the medieval Georgian kingdom.

She was called king of kings. Her generals, the Mkhargrdzeli brothers, defeated Muslim neighbours at Shamkor in 1195 and Basiani in 1202, and Georgia extended its rule over much of Armenia and parts of Shirvan. In 1204 she helped found the Empire of Trebizond on the Black Sea. Her reign saw a flowering of churches, frescoes and literature, including The Knight in the Panther's Skin and the cave monastery of Vardzia. The Georgian church made her a saint. Within a generation of her death the Mongols ended the golden age.
sum: Tamar was queen of Georgia from 1184 to 1213, the first woman to rule Georgia in her own right, whose reign marked the height of the medieval Georgian kingdom.
